tool_name: Planview Portfolios (formerly Planview Enterprise One) and Planview AgilePlace (formerly Planview LeanKit), by Planview — Strategic Portfolio Management + enterprise Kanban delivered as an integrated suite alongside Planview Hub (formerly Tasktop), ProjectPlace, and PPM Pro
target_user: Sharply split by product. Planview Portfolios is admin-led, IT-driven, and procurement-gated — sold via enterprise sales, deployed via Planview Professional Services or partners (Winmill, Ignite Technology, Acuity), and configured by a dedicated 'Planview Enterprise administrator' role responsible for structures, users, rates, calendars, tiles, dashboards, Data Mart, and extracts. Planview AgilePlace is the opposite: per-user pricing (~$20/user/month), 30-day free trial with no credit card, and board-level self-service. AgilePlace exposes a per-board role tier (Administrator / Manager / User / Reader / No Access) plus an Account Administrator, so the same user can be a Board Administrator on one board and a Reader on another. Net: Portfolios = enterprise admin/IT; AgilePlace = team-lead self-service.
setup_time_estimate: Planview Portfolios: weeks to months. Planview's Professional Services markets a 'FastTrack' analytics-first delivery model and partners advertise a 6-week rapid-deployment option for early value, while reviewers consistently describe full rollouts as taking 'months of consulting and training'. The Digital Project Manager review (2026) notes 'initial setup and configuration can be time-consuming'. Planview AgilePlace: hours to days. The vendor sells a 30-day free trial, publishes a 7-part 'Getting Started' course, and Customer Success documentation describes board creation as immediate; G2 reviewers consistently call board setup 'easy to use and setup'. A team can stand up a working AgilePlace board the same day; a Portfolios programme is an IT project.
onboarding_wizard: AgilePlace: ships a guided Getting Started experience (seven-part course in the Customer Success Center) plus a Board Template Library browser where the user picks a template, edits lanes/WIP limits, invites users, and is on a working board within minutes. There is no branching 'choose Scrum/Kanban/SAFe' wizard — AgilePlace is Kanban-centric by design and the framework choice happens at the template-selection step. Portfolios: [uncertain] no modern in-product setup wizard surfaced in research — onboarding is delivered through Planview Professional Services and the Training Academy's 'Configuring Planview Enterprise' curriculum, which targets the named administrator. The Administration documentation describes a programmatic admin model (scripted dialogs, configured screens, custom column sets, WBS templates) rather than a self-service first-run flow.
template_library: AgilePlace ships a Board Template Library with a documented 'Top 10 Board Templates' shortcut for common patterns (IT Operations, Software Development, Marketing, Personal Kanban, etc.), and Planview publishes a marketing-specific set of 8 Kanban board templates. Templates can be cloned, edited, and — via the API — created from scratch (`POST /board-template`), enabling 'repeatable processes' to be standardised across an organisation. Templates are board-scoped, not portfolio-scoped. Planview Portfolios: templates come in the form of Work Breakdown Structure (WBS) templates, scripted dialogs (for lifecycle and attribute selection), and 'configured screens' authored by an administrator — these are admin-built assets, not a community gallery. The Customer Success Center documents 'Using and Managing Board Templates' for AgilePlace and 'Configuring Planview Enterprise' for Portfolios as fundamentally different motions.
ai_assisted_setup: Planview Anvi (formerly Planview Copilot) launched late 2024 / early 2025 and was promoted heavily entering 2026 — built on Amazon Bedrock per Planview's AWS engineering case study, recognised with the 2025 Globee Silver award for SPM and the DEVOPS Tech Ascension award. Anvi delivers cross-portfolio insights, recommendations, and actions powered by Planview's 'data fabric'. As of May 2026, public collateral positions Anvi as a decision-support and productivity assistant for ongoing portfolio prioritisation, resource allocation, and scenario planning — not as a configuration / setup wizard. No published feature surfaced where Anvi authors a Portfolio structure or an AgilePlace board from a natural-language prompt; that capability — if present — is uncertain.
hierarchy_config: Two different models stitched together. Planview Portfolios uses a Portfolio → Program → Project → Work hierarchy with extensive structural metadata (Organisations, Resources, Rates, Calendars, Locations, Cost Categories, Lifecycles, Lifecycle Steps, WBS Templates) and is deliberately schema-rich for finance/resource alignment — the administrator is responsible for defining and maintaining this. Planview AgilePlace is hierarchy-light by design: it models Boards → Lanes → Cards with parent/child Card relationships across boards, optional Connections to roll up cross-board work, and the Board Template Library as the configuration surface. Connecting AgilePlace boards into Portfolios for end-to-end rollups is achieved via Planview Hub (formerly Tasktop) or Planview's native integrations, which themselves require admin/IT involvement. Setting up the Portfolios hierarchy is typically the slowest part of a Planview rollout.
multi_team_setup: Built for enterprise scale, but in two motions. AgilePlace scales by adding boards and users — self-service for board admins, unlimited boards per account, role-per-board model that lets a single AgilePlace tenant host hundreds of teams without flattening permissions. Portfolios scales via the organisational structures the administrator defines (Organisations, Programs, Lifecycles) and is the integration backbone for cross-team rollups. The integrated suite covers 1 team to 1000+ teams, but moving from single-team AgilePlace to enterprise Portfolios rollup is an admin/PS project, not a self-service upgrade — and Planview Hub is the recommended mechanism for stitching together heterogenous teams using Jira, ADO, ServiceNow, and AgilePlace simultaneously. The integrated suite (Portfolios + AgilePlace + Hub) is one of the most complete enterprise stories on the market; the seam is the procurement and PS engagement required to connect the pieces.
admin_dependency: High for Portfolios, low for AgilePlace. Portfolios documents a dedicated 'Planview Enterprise administrator' responsible for defining structures, users, rates, calendars, tiles, dashboard reports, Data Mart, extracts, configured screens, and custom column sets. AgilePlace gives Board Administrators near-full local control: they can change board layout, lanes, WIP limits, card types, user/team access, and reports for their board without touching the account admin. Account-level concerns (SSO, billing, account-wide users, board templates promoted to the library) remain account-admin tasks. Net effect: AgilePlace is the rare Planview surface where a team lead can self-serve end-to-end; Portfolios is the canonical enterprise IT-driven product.
permissions_model: AgilePlace: clean five-tier per-board model — Administrator, Manager, User, Reader, No Access — plus the account-level Account Administrator. The model is widely praised in reviews; documentation explicitly notes 'a user can be an Administrator for one board, but only a Reader for other boards', which is what makes board-level self-service workable. Planview Portfolios and ProjectPlace use a richer role/group/access-rights model documented in their respective Customer Success spaces (Spigit, ProjectPlace, Portfolios each have separate permission documentation). Reviewers describe the Portfolios permission model as powerful but complex enough that a dedicated administrator is effectively required. The split between simple AgilePlace permissions and complex Portfolios permissions is one of the most distinctive seams in the Planview suite.
import_capabilities: Planview's import/migration story is dominated by Planview Hub (formerly Tasktop, acquired 2022). Hub provides bi-directional, near real-time, no-code integration between 60+ enterprise systems including Jira, Azure DevOps, ServiceNow, IBM DOORS Next, Micro Focus ALM/QC, Polarion, and Planview's own AgilePlace and Portfolios. Hub is the recommended path for migration as well as for ongoing sync — organisations use it to consolidate Jira instances, migrate from Rally/Jira/ADO into Planview, or run Planview alongside legacy tools. Hub itself is a separate licensed product; it is not push-button self-service but is no-code. CSV and Excel imports exist at the per-board level for AgilePlace; for Portfolios, the administrator-authored 'extracts and Data Mart' pattern is the canonical bulk-data path. Self-service migration without Hub or PS is realistic only for small AgilePlace boards.
migration_story: Migrations are deliberately a Planview Hub story. Hub's positioning explicitly covers M&A consolidations, on-prem to cloud Jira moves, dual-tool environments, and integration between engineering tools and SPM. The 2026 Atlassian Marketplace listing for Planview Hub describes it as the enterprise integration backbone. Reviewers and case studies (NASCO, others) describe Planview rollouts as multi-month engagements with Planview Professional Services or partners. Implementation reviews call the experience 'time-consuming' and 'overwhelming for new teams' if approached without PS help. The vendor markets a 6-week rapid deployment as the optimistic case; reviewers describe months as the more common reality for full Portfolios deployments.
vcs_integration_setup: Indirect for both products. Neither Portfolios nor AgilePlace ships a first-class GitHub/GitLab integration in the way Jira or Linear do. AgilePlace's documented two-way sync integrations are with Jira, GitHub, and Microsoft Team Foundation Server — set up via a guided integration service. In practice, AgilePlace ↔ GitHub is commonly automated via Zapier, n8n, or Pipedream connectors for lighter use cases. For enterprise/regulated environments, Planview Hub is the canonical bridge between Git-based delivery systems and Planview boards/portfolios. Setup is therefore not 'connect GitHub in two clicks' — it ranges from a Zapier configuration (minutes, self-service) to a Hub deployment (days, admin/IT-led with licensed software).
slack_notifications_setup: [uncertain] No first-party 'AgilePlace for Slack' or 'Portfolios for Slack' application surfaced in primary research. Common patterns documented by ecosystem tools: Zapier supports triggers like 'Card Entered a Specific Lane' → Slack action; n8n and Pipedream both ship AgilePlace ↔ Slack templates including bi-directional flows (Slack message → AgilePlace card). Setup is therefore self-service for a power user but not click-to-install for non-technical team members. Account-admin would be required only if the Slack workspace itself locks down third-party app installs; per-board Slack notifications via Zapier are board-admin-level.
first_impression_ux: AgilePlace: clean, immediately useful. 30-day free trial with no credit card, the first run lets a user pick a Board Template from the library and start moving cards within minutes. Reviewers describe the UI as 'simple and intuitive with a good level of configuration' and 'easy to adapt to by both tech and non-tech folks'. Portfolios: enterprise-feeling and dense. There is no public free trial of Portfolios; access begins with a sales engagement and a demo, then an administrator-led configuration project. Reviewers describe the Portfolios UI as 'dated and clunky at times', 'overwhelming for new teams', and 'less intuitive than they'd like' — though the same reviewers note it is built for high-level decision-making rather than first-impression delight.
time_to_value: AgilePlace: days. The 30-day free trial is designed to demonstrate value before commercial commitment, the template library shortcuts the 'blank canvas' problem, and per-user pricing means a team lead can start small. Portfolios: weeks to months and dependent on Professional Services. Value lands when the WBS templates, lifecycles, organisational structure, financial categories, and Data Mart are configured to a level where executive-level roll-ups and resource forecasting are accurate — that is a project, not a day. The 6-week FastTrack option exists to compress this; absent it, multi-month timelines are the norm. The 'aha moment' for the suite is when AgilePlace team boards roll up via Hub into Portfolios investments and Anvi surfaces cross-portfolio reallocation recommendations — a state most organisations reach months into a rollout.
setup_complaints: Most common from G2, Capterra, TrustRadius, Gartner Peer Insights, and Software Advice (2026): (1) Portfolios 'initial setup and configuration is time-consuming' and 'months of consulting and training'; (2) 'Interface feels dated and overwhelming for new teams'; (3) 'Complexity challenging for new users'; (4) 'Better suited for high-level decision-making but less ideal if you want something simple and quick to roll out' (Digital Project Manager); (5) 'Costlier side' — enterprise pricing model deters smaller orgs; (6) AgilePlace: 'integration and generating tokens of existing APIs was a little bit difficult at the start'; (7) AgilePlace analytics/reporting 'might not be as advanced as some competitors'; (8) 'Application is not intuitive and takes time for new users to get acquainted' (minority view on AgilePlace).
setup_praise: Most common praise: (1) AgilePlace 'easy to use and setup boards' — 4.5/5 on Capterra (44 reviews, Mar 2026); (2) 'Out-of-the-box board templates' for IT Operations and Software Development called 'exceptional to start immediately'; (3) Per-board role model 'allows you to ensure that work is visible to everyone while limiting changes to only certain team members on specific boards' — praised for multi-team accounts; (4) 'Support provided by Planview teams is effective and quick'; (5) Portfolios: 'robust strategic portfolio planning capabilities' and 'integration backbone' for enterprise consolidation; (6) Anvi (AI assistant) praised in industry awards as 'expert guidance and intelligent actions powered by deep domain expertise and contextual data'; (7) Hub (Tasktop) widely regarded as the most mature enterprise integration hub for SPM/delivery toolchains; (8) Strong professional services and partner ecosystem (Winmill, Ignite Technology).
standout_setup_feature: The split-product model — and Planview Hub as the connector — is the differentiator. Few competitors offer a genuinely self-service team product (AgilePlace, hours to start) integrated with a genuinely enterprise portfolio product (Portfolios, months to perfect) connected by a purpose-built no-code integration hub (Planview Hub) that handles 60+ external systems. The standout 'setup moment' for an enterprise is the Hub configuration step where Jira instances, AgilePlace boards, ServiceNow records, and Portfolios investments are wired together once and produce a live cross-tool view — capability that competitors typically achieve through brittle point-to-point connectors or services-heavy custom builds. For a single team the standout moment is AgilePlace's 30-day free trial + template library, which is genuinely best-in-class for getting a team on a Kanban board the same afternoon.
servicenow_comparison: Planview and ServiceNow are direct competitors in Gartner's Magic Quadrant for Enterprise Agile Planning Tools and in the Strategic Portfolio Management category. Planview's centre of gravity is portfolio management with delivery as the spoke (Portfolios + AgilePlace + Hub); ServiceNow's centre of gravity is the Now Platform with SPM/EAP as a module that benefits from native ITSM, CMDB, financial, and employee data adjacency. Setup-wise both are admin-led at the portfolio tier and both depend on professional services for enterprise rollouts. Planview's AgilePlace gives it a genuinely team-self-service surface that ServiceNow EAP does not have an equally lightweight equivalent for. Planview Hub is more mature as a heterogenous-toolchain integration platform than ServiceNow's equivalent integration story; ServiceNow's advantage is unified onboarding and admin tooling for organisations already operating on the Now Platform. Per Gartner Peer Insights 2026 EAP rankings cited in adjacent ServiceNow research, ServiceNow EAP mindshare is 3.5% (down from 6.6% YoY); Planview AgilePlace and Portfolios collectively retain enterprise mindshare via the broader SPM positioning. Migration direction is most often Planview → ServiceNow when an organisation consolidates on the Now Platform, or ServiceNow → Planview when an organisation prioritises a best-of-breed delivery toolchain over a single-vendor platform; both moves are PS-led, not push-button.
